newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end stronger but pare early gains - Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end stronger but pare early gains - Jan 28.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Tuesday but weakened off early highs, as an early rally prompted by a weaker-than-expected U.S. economic report was offset by concern about upcoming data, analysts said.

"It was a relief type of bounce really, but there's still a lot of risks going into the week. The market's becoming more aware of them as we headed into the close so we gave off some of the gains," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with financial analysis firm I.D.E.A.
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.37 to C$107.45 to yield 7.355 percent.
The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond rose 3/32 to yield 6.94 percent. The spread between benchmark bonds narrowed to 42 basis points from 44 basis points at Monday's close.

Both U.S. and Canadian fixed-income markets rallied after a report that the U.S. employment cost index rose 0.8 percent in the fourth quarter, slightly lower than forecast. Dealers said the report initially sparked a short-covering rally.

Analysts said concern about other data due out this week, including Friday's Canadian and U.S. GDP data, helped to erode early gains. Investors are also focusing on testimony by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Thursday.
Recent strength in the Canadian dollar helped Canadian bonds to outperform in the downturn, analysts said.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.17 to C$102.00 to yield 6.717 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 5/32 to yield 6.65 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds was seven basis points, unchanged from Friday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.89 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.19 percent.
